commit_message:
[Merged] Fix issues with position lists and NEAR constraints.

FossilOrigin-Name: 16352d3654d5672cd0251db51dbe19f779373feb
pr_title: Handle FTS5 position lists and NEAR constraints safely
pr_description: Trim phrase position lists to entries satisfying NEAR constraints using lookahead readers. Write retained positions directly into the existing buffers without reallocating them, preserving reader pointers while maintaining position encoding and suppressing duplicate entries.

intro_commit_message:
Fix issues with position lists and NEAR constraints.

FossilOrigin-Name: 16352d3654d5672cd0251db51dbe19f779373feb
fix_commit_message:
Avoid a potential use-after-free in fts5. Report [bugs:/info/2026-06-08T08:45:27Z | 2026-06-08T08:45:27Z].

FossilOrigin-Name: 9c018b02dbfb071c748d540ad679a4dbdc0fb88a62988e02cb51a3403509febe
agent_reasoning: The position-list writer can grow and relocate a buffer while a lookahead reader still references its original allocation, creating a use-after-free. This snapshot lacks sqlite3Fts5PoslistSafeAppend, so the equivalent allocation-free encoding logic is applied directly in fts5ExprNearIsMatch using the available sqlite3PutVarint routine. Since the output is a subset of the input, existing buffer capacity suffices. Only ext/fts5/fts5_expr.c was edited; tests and Fossil metadata were left untouched. Whitespace checks and workspace validation passed.
